h1: The 6 Best Bluetooth Trackers for Wallets of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Bluetooth Trackers for Wallets: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 wallet tracker cards scored on thickness, ring volume, battery and network support, from Chipolo and Ridge to Tile Slim.
summary: The Chipolo CARD is the best wallet tracker overall, with Qi magnetic charging, up to a year per charge, a 2 year warranty and a choice of Apple or Google network. The Ridge Tracker Card is the stronger one for loudness and range at 95 dB and 300 ft. Spotminders is the iPhone-only slim option at 0.07 inches, while KIUP is thinnest at 0.06 inches and rings up to 120 dB.
intro: A wallet is the worst place to put an ordinary tracker, because anything thicker than a credit card turns a flat billfold into a bulging lump that pushes against your hip all day. That is the entire reason wallet tracker cards exist, and it makes thickness, not features, the first number to read on a listing.

Thickness drags a second choice behind it. A card-thin body leaves little room for a battery or a speaker, so you will pay for slimness with a rechargeable cell, a quieter ring or both. We scored six cards on the Primea framework, weighing thickness and network compatibility first, then charging convenience, ring volume and water protection.

products.name: Chipolo CARD Rechargeable Wallet Tracker
products.verdict: A slim card that runs up to a year per charge, with a two-year warranty and either network.
products.description:
Chipolo's CARD is sold in versions for Apple Find My or Google Find Hub, so a single design covers iPhone and Android wallets. It recharges on a Qi magnetic charger, which is not included, and the listing quotes up to 1 year per charge. A 2-year warranty also sets it apart from the cheaper cards in this group.

It beats Ridge by a narrow margin on battery life and warranty, while Ridge counters with a louder ringer. The compromise is the Qi pad: you need one before the first top-up, and a magnetic charger is a small recurring annoyance compared with a battery that you never touch.

Best for a daily wallet where you want brand support and low maintenance. Caveat: the listing gives no ring volume or thickness figure, so compare the dimensions with your slimmest wallet slot.

products.name: Ridge Tracker Card, Find My and Find Hub
products.verdict: A 95 dB ringer, 300 ft range and IP68 protection in a wallet card from a wallet maker.
products.description:
Ridge makes wallets, and its tracker card shows it: a 155 mAh battery rated for up to 5 months, an IP68 rating, a ringer up to 95 dB and a quoted range of up to 300 ft (90 m). It works with Apple Find My or Google Find Hub depending on the version. Most cards in this size class do not state this many figures.

It ranks second because five months is far shorter than the Chipolo's year between charges, which means more frequent plug-ins. In return you get a noticeably louder ringer than most cards here, and the range figure gives you a rough sense of the direct Bluetooth link.

A good fit if your wallet tends to hide in a bag or a car. Caveat: treat the 300 ft range as open-air best case, since pockets and walls shorten it a lot.

products.name: Spotminders Wallet Tracker PRO, Apple MFi Certified
products.verdict: A 0.07 inch MFi-certified card with a 100 dB speaker and up to 8 months per charge.
products.description:
Spotminders PRO is an Apple-only card certified under the MFi program, so it reports through the Find My network and iOS only. It is 0.07 inches thin, rated IP68, rings up to 100 dB and offers left-behind alerts that nudge your phone when the wallet stays behind. Battery life is quoted at up to 8 months per charge.

It ranks third because Apple-only is a hard limit; the Chipolo and Ridge both offer Android versions. In return, the MFi badge and the left-behind alerts make it the most safety-minded card for iPhone owners, and 8 months beats Ridge's 5.

Best for an iPhone household that leaves its wallet at restaurants and bars. Caveat: iOS only means a spouse on Android cannot see the card in any app.
products.idealFor: iPhone users who forget their wallet at restaurants.
products.skipIf: Anyone using the card has an Android phone.

products.name: KIUP Wallet Tracker Card 0.06in Slim
products.verdict: A 0.06 inch card with a 120 dB speaker, IP68 and UWB distance on a low price.
products.description:
KIUP's card is 0.06 inches thin, the slimmest in the roundup, with a speaker up to 120 dB, IP68 protection and Ultra Wideband distance readouts. It works with Apple Find My and Google Find Hub, and the listing claims 5 to 10 years of battery. The package is aggressive on paper: loud, thin and cheap.

It ranks fourth because the 5 to 10 year battery claim is the sort of figure that deserves skepticism for a sealed card, and the brand has less track record than Chipolo or Ridge. Where it wins is raw spec value: the loudest ringer and thinnest body together.

A sensible pick for tight wallets and shoppers on a budget. Caveat: if the battery is not replaceable or rechargeable, the card may be disposable after its life, so check how it is powered before relying on the headline claim.

products.name: UQO Wallet Tracker Card, Find My or Find Hub
products.verdict: An 85.6 x 54 x 2.85 mm card that charges in about an hour and warns on separation.
products.description:
UQO's card measures 85.6 x 54 x 2.85 mm and weighs 13.6 g, matching a standard payment card in footprint but 2.85 mm thick, so it is the chunkiest card here. It supports Apple Find My or Google Find Hub, rings at 85 dB or more and sends separation alerts. About an hour on a Qi charger is quoted to give 2 to 3 months of use.

It ranks fifth because the ringer is the quietest in the roundup and two to three months per charge means frequent top-ups. Against the Chipolo, the dimensions are published, which helps you check fit before buying, but the thickness is a real cost in a slim wallet.

A fit for roomy wallets, passport holders and travel pouches. Caveat: in a slim bifold, 2.85 mm adds noticeable bulk, so measure your slot first.

products.name: Life360 Tile Slim Wallet Tracker, iOS and Android
products.verdict: Tile's thinnest tracker, working on iOS and Android, with SOS and a family map.
products.description:
Tile Slim is the company's thinnest tracker, meant to slide into a wallet, and it works with both iOS and Android through the free Tile app and Life360. It can ring your phone even when silenced, adds a discreet SOS alert and displays a family map in Life360. Unlike the others, it does not use Apple Find My or Google Find Hub.

It ranks last because Tile's crowd network is smaller than Apple's or Google's, so recovery away from home is less likely, and the listing gives no thickness, ring volume or battery numbers. It earns its place by covering both phone types in one app.

A reasonable choice for households split between platforms who already use Life360. Caveat: with no stated specs, compare the Chipolo or Ridge card before buying if you need documented figures.

whatMatters.detail: Measured in inches or millimeters, thickness decides whether the card slides into a slot beside your cash or bulges the wallet. The KIUP at 0.06 inches and Spotminders at 0.07 are nearly invisible, while the UQO at 2.85 mm is noticeable in a slim bifold. Check the exact figure and compare it with your tightest slot.

Wallet cards report through Apple Find My, Google Find Hub or Tile, and the network decides which phones can locate the card when it is out of range. Some versions are sold per network. Check the listing for the network name and OS support, and note that an iOS-only card like the Spotminders is useless to an Android user.

Rechargeable cards need a Qi pad or similar, and months per charge range from the UQO's 2 to 3 up to the Chipolo's 12. Longer is better for a wallet you never think about, because a dead card is invisible until the day you lose the wallet. Look for the charger type, whether it is included and the stated months.

A thin card has a tiny speaker, so volume varies from the UQO's 85 dB to the KIUP's 120 dB on paper. Higher helps when the wallet is buried in a bag or coat. Look for an actual decibel figure, and remember that leather and fabric pockets muffle sound, so treat the number as a best case.

Wallets get rained on, sweated on and sat on in back pockets, and a cracked seal ends a card quickly. An IP68 rating, listed for the Ridge, Spotminders and KIUP, means dust tight and protected against continuous immersion. Check whether the listing states an actual IP number, and prefer it over vague claims of water resistance.

faq.q: Will a wallet tracker fit in a slim bifold?
faq.a: Thin cards will. The KIUP is 0.06 inches and the Spotminders 0.07 inches, close to a credit card. The UQO measures 2.85 mm and is chunkier, so check your slot depth first, especially in a tight minimalist wallet.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with wallet trackers?
faq.a: Buying an iPhone-only card for a household with Android users. The Spotminders is explicitly iOS only, while the Chipolo CARD and Ridge support Apple or Google networks, and the Life360 Tile works on both phone platforms. Check the network before you check the price.

faq.q: Is the Chipolo CARD worth it over cheaper cards?
faq.a: For daily carry, yes. It offers up to a year per charge and a 2-year warranty, which means fewer charging chores, while the UQO costs less but quotes 2 to 3 months per charge, and the KIUP battery claim is harder to verify.

faq.q: How do I charge a wallet tracker card?
faq.a: Place it on a Qi charger. The Chipolo CARD uses a magnetic Qi pad that is not included in the box, so budget for one, and the UQO quotes about an hour of charging for 2 to 3 months of use.

faq.q: Will I get an alert if I leave my wallet?
faq.a: Some cards do. The Spotminders PRO has left-behind alerts and the UQO sends separation alerts when the wallet and phone part ways. Switch notifications on in the app settings, and mark your home as a safe zone so they do not fire constantly.

faq.q: Can a wallet tracker survive rain or a pocket wash?
faq.a: IP68 cards, including the Ridge, KIUP and Spotminders, are designed to resist dust and immersion, so rain and a dropped wallet are fine. Even so, avoid putting them through a full wash cycle, where soap and heat go beyond the rating.

finalTake: The Chipolo CARD Rechargeable Wallet Tracker is the best all-round wallet tracker here, with a long battery life, a two-year warranty and a choice of network. Choose the Ridge when volume and range matter, the Spotminders if you are all-in on iPhone, and the KIUP when thinness is the priority. Check the network and thickness first, and the rest is detail.
